name: Muthoot Microfin Ltd
title: Muthoot Microfin Ltd - 544055 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Muthoot Microfin is pivoting from monoline JLG to diversified retail: FY26 AUM ₹14,005 cr (+13%), GNPA 3.89%, credit cost 3.5%, and a ₹30,000 cr AUM by 2030 target needing ~21% CAGR.

triggers.label: Cost of funds 11.02% → 10.27%
triggers.quote: We had a cost of fund of 11.02%. That cost of fund has come down to 10.27%, and it is further likely to come.

triggers.label: Collection efficiency 93% → 96.4%
triggers.quote: The collection efficiency which was around 93% has gone to around 96.4% overall.

triggers.label: Q4 disbursements ₹2,876 cr, +46% YoY
triggers.quote: we have disbursed around INR2,876 crores, which is almost 46% growth year-on-year

triggers.label: FY27 AUM growth 12–15% guided
triggers.quote: Yesterday in your presentation, your AUM growth for FY27 was 12% to 15%.

guidance.quote: Yesterday in your presentation, your AUM growth for FY27 was 12% to 15%.
Muthoot Microfin is aiming to reach INR30,000 crores AUM by 2030.
consistently delivering a ROA of 5% and above, ROE of 20% and above
we are looking at 13.5% to 14% NIM expanding.
we are likely to be 5% and below by 2030 in terms of our , sorry, operating cost.
Around four times leverage is what the company is comfortable at a balance sheet level.

prior_guidance_check.quote: In terms of AUM growth that we had guided for around 5% to 10%, we are at 13%.
the credit cost that we had guided 4% to 6%, we are much below that at 3.5%.
in terms of our diversification strategy that we were talking 85% to 15%, we are at 83% to 17%.

red_flags.quote: your AUM growth for FY27 was 12% to 15%. Now, if you take 12% to 15% growth for FY 27, the remaining three years you have to grow at a CAGR of around 23%.

red_flags.quote: We are having a rejection rate of RSI of 60% collectively

red_flags.quote: when your yields actually go up, the ability of the portfolio to perform better on credit cost usually does not happen.

summary.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q4 FY26: AUM ₹14,005 crore (+13% YoY), Q4 profit ₹71 crore, GNPA down to 3.89%; Vision 3030 targets ₹30,000 crore AUM by 2030.
summary.overview: Management used its maiden Capital Markets Day (7 May 2026) to unveil Vision 3030: ₹30,000 crore AUM, ROA of 5%+, ROE of 20%+ and 10 million lives by 2030. FY26 showed a full-year loss of ₹222 crore in the prior year turning into a ₹170 crore full-year profit, with Q4 profit of ₹71 crore described as the best in seven quarters. Asset quality improved: GNPA 3.89% (from 4.85%), net NPA 1.14%, Q4 credit cost 2.8% and FY26 credit cost 3.5%. Diversification moved non-JLG to about 17% of the portfolio, and cost of funds fell to 10.27% from 11.02%.

financial_highlights.metric: Portfolio under management (AUM) at FY26 end

financial_highlights.change: highest in last seven consecutive quarters

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 credit cost / FY26 credit cost

financial_highlights.change: from 11.02% (about 75 bps lower); incremental borrowing cost ~9.9%

segments.name: JLG (joint liability group)
segments.commentary: About 83% of the portfolio at FY26 end (82.6% per CEO); yield ~24.5% effective. Management says JLG remains the entry point and the 2030 mix targets about 53% JLG.

segments.name: Muthoot Small Enterprise Loan (individual loans)
segments.commentary: Portfolio ~₹2,383-2,387 crore with near-zero delinquency; FY26 disbursement ₹2,536 crore; monthly disbursement ₹450-470 crore; ticket ₹60,000-3 lakh at 23-25% ROI; ~90% NACH clears same day; 97% of borrowers have bureau score above 730.

segments.name: Micro-LAP / MSME LAP
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursement ~₹26.5 crore, with monthly disbursement near ₹11 crore; average ticket ~₹4 lakh; 100% collection and no delinquency as stated; ROI 18-22%; Kerala is 45% of the book.

segments.name: Gold loans (via Muthoot FinCorp referral)
segments.commentary: Referral volume ~₹7 crore per month; co-lending with Muthoot FinCorp under consideration; yield ~17-21%.

guidance_outlook: Vision 3030: AUM ₹30,000 crore by 2030, implying ~21% CAGR from ₹14,000 crore; the company says it aims for >15% growth in FY27 (management earlier cited a 12-15% range in analyst questions).
Long-run credit cost target ~2.5%; FY30 ROA target 5%+ (~₹1,000 crore profit in FY30 confirmed); ROE 20%+.
NIM: management expects FY27 NIM of roughly 12.5% and 13.5-14% (13% 'across cycles') by FY30; no credit rating upgrade assumed for FY27.
Opex to fall to 5% or below by 2030 from 6.4%; weighted average portfolio yield to rise from 18.8% to 22-23%.
Balance sheet leverage target ~4x (3.3x on balance sheet now); about 12-15 months of current capital to fund growth before equity is needed.
NCD/ECB share of borrowings to rise from 22% to ~40% by 2030; digitally collected share of collections to reach 75% by 2030 (about 40% now).
capex_capacity: Network: 1,670 branches across 21 states and UTs, 390 districts; 91 branches merged or closed under branch-profitability review, while new branches opened in Assam, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
Workforce 15,735 employees, ~90% in field roles; ~12% of field roles are female ROs, with attrition about 50% lower than male counterparts.
Credit underwriting: dedicated team of ~1,800 (about 2,000 in the credit vertical) with generative-AI-assisted credit appraisal memos.
Vision 2030 product mix: JLG 53%, individual loans ~33%, MSME LAP ~10%, retail secured ~3%.
Contingency funding of ₹2,000-3,000 crore available at short notice; ₹700-800 crore free funds carried through the year, plus HQLA.
CGFMU / CGTMSE guarantee applied for, pending budget allocation; the new CGS-MFI scheme capped at ~₹300 crore for the company.
demand_pricing: Wallet-share study: for ~30 lakh overlapping customers, FY24 to FY26 microfinance exposure fell ~32% while total loan balances rose from ~₹40,000 crore to ~₹45,000 crore; gold exposure rose from ₹4,093 crore to ₹7,456 crore.
Yields: JLG effective ~24.5%, individual loans ~23.5%, LAP 18-22%, gold 17-21%; management says micro-LAP at 27-28% due to processing fees.
Rejections: post-MFIN guardrails the JLG rejection rate is ~60% (Karnataka ~65%); productivity per employee fell to ~₹7 lakh in Q1 due to rejections.
Rural focus: 98% of branches are rural; competition described as relatively limited in these areas.
Lending rates were cut multiple times in 2024; management says ~70% of FY26 disbursements were made at rates ~200 bps lower than the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 21% CAGR to ₹30,000 crore square with FY27 guidance of 12-15%, and what gives confidence growth accelerates from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 beat four of five guidance items (AUM growth 13% vs 5-10% guided, credit cost 3.5% vs 4-6%, mix 83:17 vs 85:15) and expects more than 15% growth in FY27, with the step-up from diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Will diversification shield the company from the microfinance cycle, and what is FY30 asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification and deeper household engagement should smooth the cycle, with long-run credit cost of about 2.5%; FY30 profit of ~₹1,000 crore was confirmed as the target.

qa_highlights.question: How is underwriting done without over-reliance on talent, and why a hybrid rather than centralised model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a human-in-the-loop model: field credit officers use AI-assisted appraisal memos and aggregator data, and a central team sets loan ceilings within which branches decide.

qa_highlights.question: How do individual loans differ in credit risk from JLG, and how can the bounce and delinquency record be trusted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 0+ and 30+ delinquency of zero on ~₹2,300 crore, ~10% NACH bounce collected within eight days, a 700+ bureau score floor, and 2-3 years of repayment track record with the company.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM rise from 12% to 13-14% when new-disbursement yields are similar to the new loan rates?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 NIM was 12.8% at the start of the year and about 12% in FY26; repricing benefits from the Q2 FY26 yield changes fall into FY27, with NIM back to about 12.5%. The 13%+ level rests on mix, cost of funds and yield, and FY27 excludes any rating upgrade.

qa_highlights.question: What are branch rationalisation plans and the benefit from the CGS-MFI guarantee scheme?
qa_highlights.answer: 91 branches have been merged or closed, while new branches open in new states. CFO said the CGS-MFI scheme caps the company at ~₹300 crore and adds little for a large MFI, with cost of funds already at ~9.9% on incremental borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company charge higher yields for lower-risk products, and why would credit cost fall as yields rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the yield rise is driven by higher-yield new originations and the shrinking of the defaulting denominator, and that Muthoot's brand and gold-custody service let it price slightly higher than peers.

qa_highlights.question: What are leverage and capital needs to reach 5% ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company targets about 4x leverage (3.3x on balance sheet now), with NIM +100 bps, opex -50 bps and credit cost around 2.5% sufficient for 5% ROA, plus about 1% of fee income.

risks_watch: Dependence on the JLG segment (about 83% of AUM) and on Southern states, where 55% of customers sit; state-level regulatory risk raised by a questioner, with management saying regulated entities are exempt from local rules.
Execution risk on the ~21% AUM CAGR and on yield uplift to 22-23%; the FY27 guidance of 12-15% is below the FY30 path.
Credit quality of new individual/MSME/LAP products over a full credit cycle, since they have limited seasoning (about 2.5-3 years of track record for the cohort).
Interest rate and inflation risk: management flagged a possible modest policy-rate increase.
Equity dilution: management said equity will be needed at some point, with the current capital covering about 12-15 months of growth.
Rising rejection rates (~60%) constrain JLG sourcing and productivity; watch employee productivity and attrition.
key_quotes: So we are confident that we will overachieve our guidance.
So effectively what is happening is that whenever we do a rate change or a yield change that is always a prospective impact.
So we'll be looking at four times leverage.
So I think the idea is to have a qualitative growth and a sustainable growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and funding, with the CEO and CFO stressing that FY26 beat most guidance items and that liquidity is ample. Cautious and hedged on the 2030 path: the 21% AUM CAGR, the 5% ROA and the 13-14% NIM are framed as targets, FY27 NIM is guided lower at about 12.5%, and no rating upgrade is assumed for FY27. Evasive on state-level political risk and on the pace of the JLG shift, where answers leaned on the brand and on "not moving away from JLG".

adds.what: New branches opened in Assam, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh (offset by 91 branches merged or closed; network 1,670 branches)

growth.why: FY27 AUM growth guided at 12-15% (midpoint 13.5%) and Vision 3030 targets ₹30,000 crore AUM by 2030, backed by Q4 disbursements of ₹2,876 crore (+46% YoY), collection efficiency at 96.4% and lower cost of funds, but no specific new capacity or order book is quantified beyond branch openings net of 91 closures.
